counterfactual_missing_items: previous workup negative for antiphospholipid syndrome and protein C deficiency
No personal or family history of clotting or liver disease
Liver showed smooth contours with no signs of cirrhosis
decisive_items: 2.8-cm filling defect in the common hepatic artery
Multifocal peripheral dilation of bile ducts at right liver lobe
response.rationale: R5 is the most complete diagnosis because the arterial-phase MRI filling defect directly identifies common hepatic artery thrombosis, and the bile-duct dilation and left-lobe atrophy are secondary hepatic ischemic changes. R6 captures the thrombotic mechanism but is nonspecific and lacks the arterial anatomy and downstream liver findings. R2 explains only the presenting pyelonephritis, while R3 and R4 misattribute the imaging to biliary or hepatic venous causes rather than the arterial filling defect.

rejected.why: Bile duct dilatation is only a secondary imaging finding and does not account for the common hepatic artery filling defect.
Pyelonephritis explains the presenting flank pain and kidney imaging but not the hepatic artery filling defect or biliary/lobar changes.
Budd-Chiari syndrome requires hepatic venous outflow obstruction; the raw imaging shows a common hepatic artery filling defect, not hepatic vein thrombosis, and there is no hepatomegaly or ascites.
